title: Apply the Table II randomization in the CPU surrogate and test it against the pre-change trajectory
summary: The CPU surrogate takes --randomization none|table2_v1 in training and evaluation. Under table2_v1 each replica owns a MuJoCo model copy and redraws its link masses, payload, foot friction, gains, motor strength, reset pose and push schedule from the Step 7 declaration at every reset; run identities bind the declaration hash and resume refuses a different one. The AMP adapter fills the critic's friction and push slots from the environment. A committed extract of the pre-change trajectory step7_baseline_20261013_001 (main 7478fca8) shows that none reproduces every state row bit for bit, including a selected reset. Tests cover draw bounds, determinism, replica isolation, the 1.6 N m motor cap, resume mismatch, the privileged layout and actor isolation, and pin the bytes of the historical records and the approved model. A fresh self check at revision 232e19f0 passes without native references.
next: Train two surrogate runs from seed 20260917, none against table2_v1 for 2000 updates, add the 27-cell fixed-condition sweep and bring both to the first #67 review, which freezes the ranges and push schedule before any native code.
reason: CPU design evidence only: no native run, admission or accepted capability changes.
